diagnosis: Pulmonary tuberculosis with newly diagnosed HIV

patient.name: Nomvula Dlamini
patient.personality: soft-spoken, worried, minimises symptoms unless asked directly
patient.openingLine: Doctor, I've had this cough that just won't go away...

presentingComplaint: 6-week productive cough with weight loss and night sweats

history.fact: Cough started about 6 weeks ago and has gradually worsened
Cough is productive of yellow sputum; twice noticed streaks of blood
Drenching night sweats for the past month — has to change her nightdress
Lost about 6 kg over 2 months without dieting; clothes hang loose
Feels feverish most evenings, has not measured it
Gets short of breath climbing the hill to the taxi rank, which is new
Never tested for HIV; her partner was diagnosed HIV positive three months ago
Her uncle, who lives in the same household, was treated for TB last year
No previous illnesses, never been admitted to hospital, no previous TB
Takes no regular medication, only paracetamol occasionally for headaches
Never smoked, does not drink alcohol; lives in Umlazi with her mother, uncle and two children in a four-room house
Mother has high blood pressure; no family history of diabetes or cancer
No headache, no vomiting, no diarrhoea, no urinary symptoms, periods regular, no rash

examination.general: Thin, chronically unwell-looking young woman. Pallor +. No clubbing, no cyanosis, no oedema. Generalised small-volume lymphadenopathy (cervical and axillary). Oral thrush noted.
examination.respiratory: Trachea central. Right upper zone: dull to percussion with bronchial breathing and coarse crackles. No wheeze.
examination.cardio: Normal heart sounds, no murmurs, JVP not elevated.
examination.abdo: Soft, non-tender. 2 cm smooth hepatomegaly. No splenomegaly, no ascites.
examination.neuro: Alert and orientated, no meningism, grossly intact.

investigations.name: Sputum GeneXpert MTB/RIF
investigations.result: MTB detected, rifampicin resistance NOT detected

investigations.name: Chest X-ray
investigations.result: Right upper lobe consolidation with early cavitation; no pleural effusion

pathophys.night sweats: Cytokine-mediated (TNF-α, IL-1) fluctuation of the hypothalamic temperature set-point in chronic granulomatous infection
pathophys.haemoptysis: Caseating granulomas eroding into bronchial vessels; cavitation exposes vasculature
pathophys.weight loss: TNF-α (cachectin) driven catabolism plus anorexia of chronic infection, compounded by HIV wasting
pathophys.upper lobe predilection: Higher alveolar oxygen tension and reduced lymphatic clearance in the apices favour bacillary growth

staging: WHO HIV clinical stage 3 (pulmonary TB, oral candidiasis); drug-susceptible TB, new patient

definitive: Start ART ~2 weeks after TB treatment initiation (CD4 <50: within 2 weeks; otherwise within 8 weeks)
supportive: Nutritional support and grant referral if eligible
Contact tracing and household screening, including the children
Counsel on IRIS symptoms when ART starts
followUp: Monitor LFTs if symptomatic on treatment
VL and CD4 monitoring per ART guidelines

stationChecklist.item: Introduces self, confirms patient identity, gains consent
Characterises the cough (duration, sputum, haemoptysis, pattern)
stationChecklist.answer: 6 weeks, productive yellow sputum, twice blood-streaked
stationChecklist.why: Cough >2 weeks triggers TB workup in South Africa

stationChecklist.item: Screens constitutional symptoms (weight loss, night sweats, fever)
stationChecklist.answer: All present — 6 kg loss, drenching sweats, evening fevers

stationChecklist.item: Asks HIV status / offers testing; takes sexual history sensitively
stationChecklist.answer: Never tested; partner diagnosed positive 3 months ago
stationChecklist.why: HIV testing is standard of care in any SA TB presentation

stationChecklist.answer: Household uncle treated for TB last year
stationChecklist.why: Strongest single risk factor in this history

stationChecklist.item: Performs focused respiratory exam (inspection, percussion, auscultation)
stationChecklist.answer: Right upper zone dullness, bronchial breathing, coarse crackles
stationChecklist.why: Localises pathology and supports cavitary disease

stationChecklist.item: Notes general signs: wasting, pallor, lymphadenopathy, oral thrush
stationChecklist.answer: All present — thrush suggests advanced immunosuppression

stationChecklist.item: Offers ranked differential with linked reasoning (TB > CAP > bronchiectasis > malignancy)
stationChecklist.why: Symptom-to-differential reasoning is the exam philosophy

stationChecklist.item: Requests sputum GeneXpert, HIV test with consent, CXR (± CD4 once positive)
stationChecklist.why: Confirmatory pathway per SA TB guidelines

stationChecklist.item: Outlines 2HRZE/4HR, ART timing, co-trimoxazole, pyridoxine, notification, contact tracing
stationChecklist.why: Management per SA EML / TB guidelines

examinerBank.question: Before you go on, doctor — what is your differential diagnosis at this point, and what in the history drives each item?
examinerBank.modelAnswer: TB first (household contact, >2-week cough, constitutional symptoms, haemoptysis, HIV exposure risk), then community-acquired pneumonia (productive cough, fever — but the 6-week course and weight loss argue against), bronchiectasis (chronic productive cough — but no prior chest disease), and lung malignancy (weight loss and haemoptysis — but very unlikely at 28 in a never-smoker).
examinerBank.gradingNotes: Full marks: ranked differential WITH linked reasoning for each. Partial: unranked list or no reasoning.

examinerBank.question: You mentioned she reports night sweats. Walk me through the pathophysiology of night sweats in this condition.
examinerBank.modelAnswer: Chronic granulomatous infection drives macrophage release of TNF-alpha and IL-1, which act on the hypothalamus to reset and fluctuate the temperature set-point; the evening fever breaks during sleep with compensatory sweating.
examinerBank.gradingNotes: Wants mechanism (cytokines, hypothalamic set-point), not a restatement of the symptom.

examinerBank.question: Her CD4 count comes back at 187 cells per microlitre. How does that specific number change your management, and why?
examinerBank.modelAnswer: CD4 <200: start co-trimoxazole preventive therapy against PJP; ART timing — since CD4 >50, start ART within 8 weeks of TB treatment (within 2 weeks if it had been <50); heightened vigilance for other opportunistic infections; counsel about IRIS when ART begins.
examinerBank.gradingNotes: Critical thinking under new information — wants the CD4 thresholds applied, not generic 'start ART'.

examinerBank.question: Who else in this household needs attention, and under which programme?
examinerBank.modelAnswer: Household contact screening under the TB programme: symptom-screen all household members; the two children need evaluation and, if under 5 or HIV-positive and TB-free, TB preventive therapy; the partner needs HIV care linkage; the case must be notified.
examinerBank.gradingNotes: Public health thinking — contacts, TPT for the children, notification.
